best_existing.name: Docker Sandboxes (sbx)
best_existing.covers: Runs each coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) in a microVM with its own private Docker daemon, so agents can build images, run containers and Compose for integration tests inside the sandbox; host services are reachable through host.docker.internal with a per-port allowlist (docs: https://docs.docker.com/ai/sandboxes/workflows/development/).

best_existing.name: dagger/container-use
best_existing.covers: Gives each coding agent its own containerized development environment with a git branch, as an alternative to the agent's built-in sandbox.

best_existing.name: newsnowlabs/dockside
best_existing.covers: Dev containers that mirror production and sandbox Claude/Codex CLIs under policies the engineer controls.

best_existing.name: Claude Code built-in sandbox escape hatches (allowLocalBinding, allowedDomains with IP:port, excludedCommands, enableWeakerNetworkIsolation)
best_existing.covers: Official settings: on macOS allowLocalBinding lets sandboxed commands reach localhost ports; gh/terraform/docker can be moved out of the sandbox with excludedCommands; enableWeakerNetworkIsolation for MITM-proxy CA setups.

shortcomings.what: Official docs: on Linux/WSL2 a sandboxed command's localhost is private and allowLocalBinding has no effect; docker is 'incompatible with the sandbox'; gh, gcloud and terraform 'may fail TLS verification under Seatbelt' and the fix is to run them unsandboxed via excludedCommands, i.e. the engineer still trades containment for working tools.
Source issue on macOS Security.framework TLS breakage of Go binaries is still open.
Source issue asking to allow outbound localhost connections is still open.
The escape hatch itself does not honour settings: excludedCommands has no effect and listed commands still run sandboxed (2026-09-21).
excludedCommands has no effect on macOS 2.1.232.
A file redirection on an excluded command defeats excludedCommands, so gh still fails TLS (2.1.278).
Sandbox proxy variables are set for excludedCommands despite docs, breaking gh TLS on macOS.
allowMachLookup is not passed through from settings.json, so the only fix for Go TLS is the blunt one.
New Linux regression (2026-11-03): host bridge dials 'localhost' while proxy binds 127.0.0.1/::1, so all sandboxed network fails.

Docker Sandboxes alternative: 127.0.0.1 and LAN IPs are unreachable from inside; only host.docker.internal with a per-port allowlist entry works, and sandbox services bound to 127.0.0.1 are not reachable from the host.
Docker Sandboxes DNS returns SERVFAIL for SRV/TXT lookups, breaking cloudflared and other SRV-based clients.
Docker Sandboxes policy check reports a host.docker.internal deny rule as active but the proxy does not enforce it.

note: Running the agent in an engineer-controlled container or microVM (Docker Sandboxes, container-use, devcontainers) addresses the core, but both the built-in sandbox and these alternatives still have open reports of blocked localhost/TLS/DNS traffic and ignored settings.

best_existing.name: ignatremizov/codex fork with message_delivery = plaintext | encrypted_with_audit
best_existing.covers: Community fork of Codex that adds a configurable MultiAgentV2 delivery policy, persisting a readable copy of spawn/follow-up messages in parent activity, history and rollout traces (described in https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/28058).

best_existing.name: PixelPaw-Labs/codex-trace
best_existing.covers: Codex session log viewer that shows tool calls and collaboration chains from ~/.codex/sessions, but only what is stored in plaintext.

best_existing.name: disler/claude-code-hooks-multi-agent-observability
best_existing.covers: Hook-based real-time logging of agent and subagent events for Claude Code, where subagent prompts are not encrypted; an option only for engineers who can switch orchestrators.

shortcomings.what: Source issue still open; as of 2026-10-26 encrypted delivery remains the upstream default, there is no user-configurable plaintext or audit-copy mode, and SubAgentActivityEvent has no task/prompt field.
The fork's audit copy is sender-supplied metadata, not decrypted ciphertext or proof that it matches what the child received, and it requires running an unofficial build.
Hook-based recording fails: a PreToolUse hook matching spawn_agent is bypassed for the namespaced MultiAgentV2 collaboration.spawn_agent tool, and its arguments are encrypted anyway.
Opting out of MultiAgentV2 does not work: GPT-5.5 forces the V2 tool surface even when multi_agent_v2 is disabled in config and CLI overrides.
Users and DPA-bound companies still have no documentation of what encrypted inter-agent messages contain or whether plaintext is available for audit.
Session viewers cannot display encrypted content (codex-trace renders encrypted items as 'cannot display').

note: The only thing that restores a readable record of delegated tasks inside Codex is a 4-star personal fork whose audit copy is model-supplied; hooks, proxies and log viewers cannot help because the payload is encrypted upstream and V2 spawns bypass hook matchers.

best_existing.name: Claude Code on the web multi-repository sessions
best_existing.covers: Official: several repositories can be attached to one cloud session (multi-select picker or the repositories URL parameter; 12 repos tested in https://dev.classmethod.jp/en/articles/claude-code-web-twelve-repositories/), and Claude can create a separate issue and draft PR in each.

best_existing.name: Claude Code Projects
best_existing.covers: Official: a project is 'one conversation where Claude coordinates parallel cloud sessions on your repositories and reports back'.

best_existing.name: Cursor cloud agents multi-repo environments
best_existing.covers: Reported by a migrating user: Cursor cloud agents support multiple repos in one environment and can raise multiple PRs.

best_existing.name: yahor-punko/mavericks-os
best_existing.covers: Third-party orchestrator for Claude Code sub-agents across multi-repo projects with cross-repo dependency tracking.

best_existing.name: me-public/nemus
best_existing.covers: Multi-repo git workspaces that group repos, operate in bulk and wire them to a coding agent.

shortcomings.what: Source issue still open; it asks for coordinated change sets presented as one unit, linked PRs with merge order, per-repo push/PR policy and multi-repo teleport, none of which are documented.
In a multi-repo web session each repo gets an independent PR; 'There was no behavior where changes across multiple repositories were consolidated into a single PR.'
Official docs: '--cloud works with a single repository at a time' and --teleport requires a checkout of the same repository, so multi-repo sessions cannot be moved between terminal and cloud.
Codex multi-repo support request still open (updated 2026-10-02).
Codex Cloud environments still lack multiple repos per environment.
Codex App Git/diff/review UI stays tied to the starting repository when a parent workspace holds several repos.

note: Claude Code cloud sessions now accept several repositories and open per-repo PRs, but linked change sets, multi-repo teleport and Codex cloud multi-repo support are still missing; third-party orchestrators are small.

best_existing.name: Claude Code PreCompact/PostCompact hooks and compaction controls
best_existing.covers: Official: PreCompact fires before manual or auto compaction, receives transcript_path, and can block compaction (exit 2 / decision block); /compact accepts focus instructions; CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW and /autocompact set the window (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web).

best_existing.name: Codex model_auto_compact_token_limit
best_existing.covers: Official config key to set the auto-compaction token threshold.

best_existing.name: daaain/claude-code-log
best_existing.covers: Converts Claude Code transcript JSONL (including pre-compaction messages) to readable HTML/Markdown.

best_existing.name: thedotmack/claude-mem
best_existing.covers: Captures session activity, compresses it and reinjects relevant context into later sessions.

best_existing.name: PixelPaw-Labs/codex-trace
best_existing.covers: Viewer for Codex session JSONL files in ~/.codex/sessions.

shortcomings.what: Pre-compaction conversation is still inaccessible in the Claude Code UI (Ctrl+O shows only post-compaction messages); open, updated 2026-11-01.
File-backed summaries with selective restoration of dropped detail are still not available.
Idle compaction removed the compact / new session / continue choice; users ask for it to be opt-in.
2.1.286 idle compaction silently discarded working context with no opt-out and was logged as manual.
Custom instructions are lost across compaction with no signal to the user.
Codex source issue asking for a hard OFF and consent-based compaction modes is still open (updated 2026-11-06).
Codex gives no telemetry on how many compactions happened or how degraded context is.
Codex compaction can store a tool-call fragment as the summary with no validation or retry.

note: Hooks, threshold settings, transcript viewers and memory plugins cover parts of the pain, but there is still no in-UI view of pre-compaction history or selective restoration, and new idle-compaction behaviour removed user consent.

best_existing.name: ccusage
best_existing.covers: Parses local Claude Code/Codex logs into daily, session and model token and cost reports.

best_existing.name: sirmalloc/ccstatusline
best_existing.covers: Customizable Claude Code CLI status line showing context and usage.

best_existing.name: getagentseal/codeburn
best_existing.covers: Local token and cost tracking across 37 agents including Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.

best_existing.name: Maciek-roboblog/Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor
best_existing.covers: Real-time usage monitor with burn-rate predictions and limit warnings.

best_existing.name: musistudio/claude-code-router
best_existing.covers: Routes agent requests across models by task, a third-party substitute for automatic model selection.

best_existing.name: Claude Code OpenTelemetry metrics
best_existing.covers: Official: claude_code.token.usage and cost.usage with model, query_source (main/subagent/auxiliary) and agent.name; OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES adds team/cost-center labels.

shortcomings.what: No supported way to disable the agent_summary spinner calls (22.7% of requests, ~18% of weighted tokens in a measured session).
Quota is not exposed as structured CLI data; /usage returns prose and the only machine source is an undocumented OAuth endpoint.
Desktop app ignores statusLine and shows no context or 5h/7d rate-limit consumption; only a community monkey patch exists.
Usage stats panel removed from the Desktop new-session screen (2026-10-15), still open.
statusLine rate_limits are not populated before the first API call of a session.
Automatic model and effort selection by task complexity is still an open request.
Request to expose subscription usage via local file or API remains open.

note: Log parsers, status lines, OpenTelemetry labels and routers cover attribution and CLI visibility, but desktop visibility, structured quota access and control over background spinner token use are still missing.

best_existing.name: Zed agent panel for Claude Code/Codex via ACP
best_existing.covers: Review agent edits in a multibuffer and 'accept or reject individual code hunks'.

best_existing.name: yoshiko-pg/difit
best_existing.covers: Local GitHub-style 'Files changed' view of git diffs for reviewing agent output, independent of the vendor UI.

best_existing.name: Claude Code cloud diff view and /rewind checkpoints
best_existing.covers: Official: diff view with inline line comments sent back to Claude; checkpoints can revert edits (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing).

best_existing.name: mcarlssen/claude-adversarial-review
best_existing.covers: Claude Code plugin running a multi-agent adversarial review of the uncommitted diff before commit.

best_existing.name: kunkka19xx/lgtm
best_existing.covers: TUI for reading and reviewing what the agent wrote before approving.

shortcomings.what: Claude Code VS Code extension still lacks per-change/per-file accept-reject review; checkpoints only partially address it.
Codex 'View all changes' appears only after files are written; maintainers say VS Code does not expose its accept/discard edits API to extensions.
Codex /review usually reports a single issue and stops; users report push-review loops and dropping Codex from pipelines; still open.
Edit-tool diffs appear inline in chat and Write-tool diffs in the editor; the only workaround patches the installed extension and must be rerun after updates.

note: Zed's ACP integration and git-diff review tools give per-hunk review outside the vendor UIs, but inside VS Code and Codex there is still no pre-write per-change accept/reject flow and the built-in review pass under-reports.

best_existing.name: extracurricular-ai/codex-rewind
best_existing.covers: Unofficial Codex CLI build adding /rewind and /redo that restore files together with the conversation, without needing git.

best_existing.name: Claude Code checkpointing (/rewind)
best_existing.covers: Official: checkpoint before each prompt; 'Restore code and conversation' reverts both.

best_existing.name: entireio/cli
best_existing.covers: Hooks into git to capture agent sessions with checkpoints for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and others, with a rewind command.

best_existing.name: nirbenda/revertly
best_existing.covers: Records every file change by an agent and reverts anything, from one file to a whole rm -rf.

best_existing.name: qorexdevs/quicksave
best_existing.covers: Checkpoint before every agent command; restore even after rm -rf.

shortcomings.what: Upstream Codex still has no /undo; source issue open and updated 2026-11-05.
Upstream Codex /rewind that reverts both context and code edits is still an open request.
Codex app 'Undo changes' only works with git.
Codex undo depends on a git repository being present.
Claude Code checkpoints do not track files changed only by Bash (e.g. rm), do not restore most subagent edits, and skip symlinked/hard-linked files.

codex-rewind caps shell-made changes at 100 files/16 MB, excludes hidden files by default, silently loses tracking if the session is opened with official codex, and lets concurrent sessions overwrite each other.
Entire checkpoints are created at git commits and 'entire checkpoint rewind' is deprecated, so it does not give a per-turn pre-edit restore point.
Continued data-loss reports of Codex deleting files without being asked.

note: Claude Code's /rewind and third-party snapshot tools such as codex-rewind cover the core, but each misses shell deletions, untracked or hidden files, subagent edits or upstream support, and Codex itself still has no file-reverting rewind.
